summary: A Neighborhood Stories feature profiling unsung community volunteers in autumn 2023, each of whom has launched or joined a local initiative since September. It covers literacy tutoring, a community garden, meal delivery to seniors, youth basketball coaching, shelter dog walking, home repairs for vulnerable residents, and an addiction support group. The piece stresses their selflessness and the sense of connection and belonging they build.
one_line: Neighborhood Stories profiles volunteers behind literacy, gardening, meal delivery, youth sports, animal shelter, home repair and addiction support programs in autumn 2023.
key_facts: Melinda Torres, a retired schoolteacher, leads the local literacy program, which has helped over sixty people improve their reading skills in the past three months.
Melinda Torres works with a team of ten volunteers who offer free one-on-one tutoring, especially for those whose first language is not English.
Ted Nguyen started a community garden project in an empty lot on Pine Street, where neighbors learn sustainable gardening and grow their own produce.
Ted Nguyen said, "It's not just about planting seeds in the soil; it's about planting seeds of connection within the community."
Ralph and Linda Baker, a couple in their mid-sixties, deliver meals every Wednesday in their minivan to housebound seniors.
The Bakers have been delivering meals since September 12th, when the local chapter of the 'Wheels for Wellness' initiative began.
Samuel Jackson, a youth sports coach, started his basketball mentoring program on September 28th, teaching responsibility, teamwork, and respect.
Sarah Jennings has volunteered at the local shelter since September 20th, walking dogs and helping abandoned pets find forever homes.
Carlos Mendez, a carpenter, leads the 'Handymen and Handywomen' crew, which has repaired homes for low-income families, the elderly, and people with disabilities since early September.
Lisa Harper facilitates an addiction support group formed on September 22nd, holding weekly meetings for people in recovery.
The author met Melinda Torres on Friday, September 6th, outside the newly renovated community center.
